extracted.intended_audience: peer reviewers, grant reviewers, research administrators, and researchers (CIHR module participants)
extracted.subtask_description: A curated bibliography of literature and resources used in CIHR's 'Bias in Peer and Merit Review' training modules, organized by topic (types of bias, peer-review process, and mitigation strategies). Intended to support education, policy development, and evidence-based interventions on bias in research funding and publishing.

rubrics_metrics.name: Bias in General
rubrics_metrics.description: This section lists foundational references that introduce general concepts of bias used throughout the Bias in Peer and Merit Review Modules (e.g., implicit bias, microaggressions, privilege, intersectionality, accessibility, and EDI best practices).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Contains books, systematic reviews, policy reports, and web resources (examples include Banaji on implicit attitudes, Kirwan Institute reviews, AAMC unconscious bias resources, CIHR publications, and Statistics Canada reports) to ground module content and provide background evidence and examples.

rubrics_metrics.name: Racial Bias
rubrics_metrics.description: References specifically addressing racial bias and systemic racism relevant to academia, research funding, publishing, and healthcare (including empirical studies, commentaries, and policy analyses).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Includes studies documenting racial disparities in funding and publication, analyses of structural racism in journals and institutions, and scholarship calling for race-conscious approaches and anti-racism interventions (examples: Erosheva et al., Hoppe et al., Merchant et al., Dzirasa, and related reviews and commentaries).

rubrics_metrics.name: Bias against Indigenous Peoples and communities
rubrics_metrics.description: References focused on Indigenous-specific issues in research and academia, including decolonizing methodologies, Indigenous-led partnerships, ethical conduct guidelines (TCPS2), and experiences of Indigenous scholars and communities.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Includes government engagement guides, Indigenous research methods literature, ethical policy documents (Tri-Council Policy Statement), and studies/reports on Indigenous participation in peer review and academic life to inform culturally appropriate and ethical review practices.

rubrics_metrics.name: Ableist Bias
rubrics_metrics.description: References concerning ableism and disability-related bias in academic and healthcare contexts, including accessibility, disclosure, accommodations, and the social vs medical models of disability.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Cites resources such as ABA materials on disability bias, Disability Language Style Guides, qualitative studies of disabled scientists, reports on accessibility experiences, and scholarship on ableism in academia to inform inclusive review practices and accommodations.

rubrics_metrics.name: Language, Institutional, Age and Career Stage Bias
rubrics_metrics.description: References dealing with biases tied to language (e.g., minority-language scholarship), institution, age, and academic career stage — factors that can affect publication, citation, and funding outcomes.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Includes studies and reports on French-language scholarship in minority contexts, linguistic bias in reviewing, publication/citation patterns by institution and career stage, government supports for official-language minority communities, and related evidence documenting disparities.

rubrics_metrics.name: Bias in the Peer Review Process
rubrics_metrics.description: References that specifically examine bias within peer review and grant review systems (e.g., gender, race, nepotism, positive-outcome bias, conservatism, reviewer selection, and reliability/validity of review).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Draws on empirical analyses, randomized trials, methodological critiques, and disciplinary studies (examples include Lee et al. 2013 on bias in peer review, Wennerås & Wold on nepotism/sexism, studies on reviewer demographics and outcome biases) to characterize how bias manifests in review processes.

rubrics_metrics.name: Ways to Mitigate Bias
rubrics_metrics.description: References that evaluate or propose interventions, strategies, and institutional policies to prevent or reduce bias in peer review, hiring, funding, and academia more broadly.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Includes randomized trials of bias-reduction interventions, scoping and systematic reviews of mitigation strategies, recommendations for inclusive metrics and anti-racism interventions, and toolkits/guides (examples: Carnes et al., Tricco et al., Moss-Racusin et al., PLOS Biology on inclusive metrics) to support actionable change.
